visual_action: The video starts with a close-up shot of Donald Trump speaking. It then cuts to a montage of various large-scale protests against him. The montage includes aerial and ground-level shots of massive crowds marching in city streets, including what appears to be Times Square in New York City and streets in Washington D.C. near the Capitol building, as well as gatherings in parks. Protesters are shown holding numerous signs with anti-Trump messages, waving American flags, and carrying effigies.

cast.name: Donald Trump
cast.evidence: He is shown speaking at the beginning of the video, and his statement is the premise for the rest of the video, which features protests against him.

on_screen_text.text: HUMPTY TRUMPTY YOU'RE DESTINED TO HAVE A GREAT FALL!
NO ONE IS ABOVE THE LAW
WE THE PEOPLE WILL NOT FORGET THE TRAITORS IN CONGRESS WHO KEPT QUIET

spoken_summary: Donald Trump says, "The demonstrations were very small, very ineffective." The rest of the video has no speech, only a rock song playing with lyrics like "No change, I can't change... but I'm here in my home... I'm a million different people from one to the next."
audio_music: The video begins with only Donald Trump's voice. After his quote, an iconic, sweeping orchestral rock track ('Bitter Sweet Symphony' by The Verve) begins abruptly and plays for the remainder of the video, creating a powerful and defiant tone that contrasts with Trump's dismissive statement.
editing_pacing: The video starts with a single, static shot of a talking head and then transitions into a fast-paced montage with quick cuts between numerous different clips of protests.
cultural_references: The song 'Bitter Sweet Symphony' by The Verve.
The nursery rhyme character 'Humpty Dumpty' is referenced in a sign reading 'Humpty Trumpty'.
central_claim: Donald Trump's assertion that protests against him are small and ineffective is demonstrably false, as shown by footage of massive crowds across the country.
intended_effect: To mock Donald Trump's statement and to energize his opponents by showcasing the vast scale and power of the popular movement against him.
